APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF DECEMBER 15, 2020

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:06 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – excused absence
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  Item 13.1 has been pulled.

  m) Mayor Pro Tem Morales
  s) Councilmember Puente  3-0 (Mayor Ancona absent)

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.
  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of December 3, 2020

All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
agenda.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

Adali Gutierrez – Vote for Irma Zamorano for City Council.

Mary Morales - I understand that you are going to decide on a new member of the City
Council this evening. A lady that you might like to consider to add to your Council is Irma
Zamarano. She has worked hard for this community for many years. She has been on
the Mountain View School District, worked on various commissions/ committees and
been an advocate for the children and citizens of El Monte for years. I know that she
would like a chance to continue to serve the community as a City Council member.
Please take her under your consideration. Thank you.

Malik Tariq Mahmood Murrabi – In the name of Allah the Gracious, The Merciful. This is
Malik Tariq Mahmood Murabbi Silsilah (Religious Minister) of Ahmadiyya Muslim
Community Respected Mayor! I'm so grateful to you and your team for giving me this
opportunity. As everybody is worried because of covid19, apart from the precautions and
the vaccine, we should turn to God. If He protects nothing can harm us and nothing can
protect us if we aren't under his protection. I want to present a few words of a man of
God, who was sent by God in this era as a non-law bearing prophet, the Promised
Messiah and Imam Mahdi. I refer to Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian, India, the
founder of Ahmadiyya Muslim Community. His Holiness says:- 1 say truly that if crying
before God Almighty is full of utmost humility, it moves His grace and mercy and draws
them (towards the supplicator). I can say out of my own experience that I have felt the
grace and mercy of God coming towards me, which comes in the shape of the
acceptance of prayer. Indeed, I rather say that I have actually seen it... More so because
I am ready to demonstrate the acceptance of prayer at all times. [Malfuzat, vol. I, p. 198].

Andres Gomez – Good evening El Monte city council, First foremost I want to say
Congratulations on the new mayor Jessica Ancona, Councilwoman Victoria Martinez

  4
   City Council Meeting Minutes of December 3, 2020

Muela and Alma Puente. Now that there's a city council vacated seat is open. I highly
recommend the city council to appoint Gabriel Ramirez for city council seat. Gabriel is
well known community leader who has attended and speak at city council meetings
addressing the issues like the affordable housing, campaign finance reform and other
issues that the city is still facing. He is a leader we need in city council who will continue
to advocate and work for the people.

Francisco Villa - Dear City Council, Congratulations on the newly mayor Jessica Ancona,
re-elected councilwoman Victoria Martinez Muela and newly elected councilwoman Alma
Puente. Now that there's a vacant seat that was left by Jessica Ancona who is now the
mayor. I would like the city council to appoint Irma Zamorano as council. Irma was a
former Mt View School Board member who has a proven record of helping students, and
parents to get the resources they need. We need leaders like Irma, I really hope you
consider appointing Irma Zamorano.

Estella Luna – I would like to see Irma Zamarano appointed to city council, filling Mayor
Acona’s seat. Irma, loves and cares for the people of El Monte. Born and raised in El
Monte has gotten to know the city and the people. She has played a major part as an
activist looking out for what’s best for the people and the city and accepting nothing in
return. She’d be an asset to the city. I would hope you would consider Irma Zamarano

Reveca Chavez - I have been a resident of El Monte for over 25 Years. I’m emailing you
in favor to support Irma Zamorano as our next City Council member. I have seen her
and know how hard she has worked for the community. She has volunteered among the
schools within our districts from elementary schools to high schools and has been
involved with parents like myself, trying to encourage, help, build and edify our
community. She has been a voice for those who cannot speak up. She has a heart for
the best interest of our City! I know she will make an excellent choice to be appointed as
our next City Council member. Please consider Irma Zamorano for City Council. She is a
great fit with the best interest for the people of El Monte City. That's what our city needs,
change and she should be part of the change that is already in progress with our new
City Mayor. Thank you for your time and consideration in giving Irma Zamorano the
opportunity to show the city the love and best interest she has for us. For any further
questions, please do not hesitate to call or email me back. Thank you and have a
wonderful evening.

Rose Chavez - I have been a resident of El Monte for 21 years. I'm emailing you in
support of Irma Zamorano as our next City Council member. I have seen her work in the
community, and volunteer at schools I attended through K-12, so I know she is someone
who actively seeks involvement with the community and is a hands on person. She is a
genuine leader, and has a heart filled with passion for keeping the best interest of the
community in mind, coming from the city herself. I am confident she will be able to fulfill
her duties as a City Council member. Have a great rest of your day, and Happy
Holidays!

Elva Leon - I am emailing to express my support to appoint Mrs. Zamorano to the City
Council seat. I currently work as a teacher for the El Monte City School District, and as a
teacher I see the need for dedicated and passionate citizens to contribute their talents,
ideas, creativity and time to the city. I have seen how Mrs. Zamorano has gone above
and beyond for the city she loves so much. Mrs. Zamorano will truly be a wonderful fit in
a city council lead by strong, determined and dedicated women.

  5
   City Council Meeting Minutes of December 3, 2020

Roberto Rios – I am a resident of El Monte, California. I have been in El Monte for 50
years and my comment for tonight is if you can please put my name in there as a vote
for Irma Zamorano. I would like for the City Council to consider being appointed seat to
replace Jessica’s seat. I would like for it to be appointed by the City Council and it would
be better if we do it that way instead of wasting money on running another run-off
election it would be best to be considered this way. I am calling because I want to
appoint Irma Zamorano and I will support her 100 percent. This is the year of the
women therefore I ask that you appoint Irma Zamorano so that we can have all women
on the City Council.

Mike Gomez – Good evening, Mayor Pro Tem and city council members. My name is
Mike Gomez and I have been in El Monte resident for over 35 years. I am using my
public comment to ask a few questions about a situation I recently read about. Mayor
Jessica Ancona stated on her Facebook page yesterday, that she tested positive for
COVID-19, something that we are sorry to hear about, and of course, hope that she
soon recovers. But in the interest of public transparency and safety, and for the sake of
the welfare of our city staff, I’d like to ask a few questions: 1). When did Mayor Ancona
test positive for COVID-19? 2). When did Mayor Ancona informed the city and city staff
that she had indeed tested positive for COVID-19? 3). What mitigation efforts has the
city taken since finding out that Mayor Ancona has tested positive for Covid-19? 4).
Again, The reason for the questions and the main concern here is regarding the safety of
our staff and to make sure that we as a city are taking every precaution to mitigate
exposure for our city staff and residents. We hope that Mayor Ancona Recovers soon
and that no one else was exposed. Thank you.

Irma Zamorano – Good evening Mayor and City Council my name is Irma Zamorano.
Honorable City Councilmembers, residents, colleagues, and friends. It is with great
humility that I ask you tonight to support my appointment to the El Monte City Council.
For 30 years I have dedicated myself to raising educational standards, advocating for
our residents and bettering our community in any way possible. During my tenure at the
Mt. View School District I pushed for expansion of special education opportunities. While
serving on the District English Language Advisory Committee I had brought in
opportunities for El Monte’s Spanish speaking residents. When I served on the School
Site Council I oversaw the budget of elementary, junior high and high school in El Monte.
I have the proven track record necessary to lead our City. As an El Monte City
Councilmember I will champion rent control, affordable housing, campaign finance
reform and Police reform. I do not now or will I ever bow to special interest. I am here to
advocate for the disenfranchised, for our undocumented brothers and sisters, for our
food insecure brothers and sisters, for our rent insecure brothers and sisters, and for all
of those experiencing hardship in our City. Please support my appointment. Thank you
and God bless you all.

Veronica Tomas – A long-time resident. During the election I got to know some of the
candidates and would like to ask the City Council to consider Irma Zamorano or Gabriel
Ramirez to fill the vacancy. Gabriel has run for Council and obtained a good amount of
votes. Irma is a great community advocate and is known for helping others in the
community and fighting corruption.

Ms. Flores – I am calling in regards appointment to the Council seat to elect Irma
Zamorano.
